decisions.reason: An adjustable quarter-pallet shelf display sits close to the core offer and costs little to keep in the catalog, and its value is still uncertain after only one year, so the option is worth holding.
The pegboard-back display is a low-cost variant on existing production lines with demand not yet resolved, so keeping the option open is cheap.
A standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a core catalog item with minimal carrying cost and no evidence of failure.
The eighth-pallet display fills a size gap in the core range cheaply, and its prospects remain open.
The wooden pallet departs from cardboard production and carries higher costs, but uncertainty has not yet resolved and it diversifies a narrow range, so it is kept for now.
The media-product display serves a niche, possibly declining segment, but it costs little to keep and its results are still open.
